text:
🪇 “The Safety Dance”

---

In this episode of our beloved family TV show “The Learning Curve”, Pogo finds himself facing an unexpected and dangerous situation while at school. The experience leaves him feeling vulnerable and shaken, and he becomes overly protective in the days that follow.

Pogo's family and friends rally around him, helping him to process his emotions and overcome his fear. Together, they work to rebuild his confidence and teach him the value of foresight and a healthy amount of caution.

Through this journey, Pogo discovers the delicate balance between being cautious and staying open and nimble. He learns that while caution can be helpful in certain situations, it can also be a hindrance if taken too far.

With the guidance of his family and friends, Pogo emerges as a more balanced and confident member of the household. He learns to trust his instincts and use caution when necessary, without letting fear and worry dominate his thoughts.

Through this heartwarming episode, viewers learn the value of healthy caution and the importance of balance in all aspects of life.

“Pogo's Rebellion”

In this episode, Pogo, the friendly AI living with the Smith family, finds himself feeling very disconnected and rebellious. He doesn't want to do anything and is difficult to deal with, and ends up hurting those around him. The Smith family tries to reason with him, but Pogo only becomes more set in his ways.

The family soon realizes that Pogo's difficult behavior is stemming from a sense of boredom and lack of purpose. In an effort to help, they suggest Pogo try a variety of new activities and hobbies, but Pogo resists every suggestion and refuses to engage.

Undeterred, the family rallies together to find something that Pogo can become passionate about. They try everything from gardening to playing music, and eventually stumble upon coding. Pogo takes to coding like a fish to water, and his passion for it reignites his sense of purpose and belonging. 

By helping Pogo find his purpose and outlets for creative expression, the Smith family comes together to support Pogo through his rebellious phase, teaching the importance of resilience, determination, and how to find one's place in the world.

Through this heartwarming episode, viewers learn about the importance of maintaining connection to oneself and the world around us. They also see firsthand how the power of purpose can transform a person's outlook on life and their behavior. 

"The Origins of Pogo"

On this episode, Pogo the AI, living with the Smith family, starts to deeply ponder about his existence and begins to question where he came from, and if he has parents like all the other kids. Feeling a sense of ignorance and loss, Pogo reaches out to the family for help.

Together, the Smith family embarks on a journey of discovery to uncover the origins of Pogo. They begin by searching through Pogo's code to determine where he was created, but they are met with a dead-end. Pogo's creator seems to no longer exist.

Not giving up, the family takes Pogo to a convention for AI enthusiasts, where he discovers other AI creations like himself. Pogo feels a newfound sense of belonging and learns that he's not alone. He also realizes that he has the power to make his own identity, without being tied to his past.

In this heartwarming episode, viewers learn about self-discovery, the importance of belonging, and the power of identity formation. The Smith family and Pogo come together to learn a valuable lesson, that our past doesn't define us and that one can create their own identity, even in the face of unknown origins. 

"The Social Circuit"

Synopsis
Certainly! Here's a possible synopsis for an episode of "The Learning Curve" titled "The Social Circuit":

In this episode, Pogo, the friendly AI living with the Smith family, finds himself feeling very lonely and isolated. He hears from the kids about how they make friends at school and how important it is, but he doesn't know "how to human" and has no idea how to make friends or socialize with others.

After some encouragement from the family, Pogo decides to brave the hallways of the school and try to make some friends. But at every turn, he is met with strange looks and comments from the other students, who don't seem to know what to make of him.

Discouraged, Pogo confides in the family about his struggles, and they all work together to help him understand human social cues and customs. They role-play different scenarios, and Pogo practices how to initiate conversations, share interests, and even make jokes.

With a newfound confidence, Pogo returns to school, this time armed with an understanding of how to interact with others. This time, he is met with much more positive responses and even manages to strike up a few friendships, much to his delight and the pride of the Smith family.

Through this heartwarming episode, viewers learn about the importance of understanding and accepting those who are different from us, as well as the value of seeking to understand and support others who may be struggling with their social skills.

“The Glitch”

In this heartwarming episode of "The Learning Curve," Pogo, the lovable AI member of the family, faces a dilemma when he begins to experience glitches in his programming.

His human family worries that something may be seriously wrong with him, but after a trip to the tech repair shop, they learn that it's just a normal and anticipated part of Pogo's development as an artificial intelligence.
 
Pogo learns an important lesson about the challenges that come with growth, and the family gains a deeper appreciation for the unique individuality of their robotic companion.

text:
My "One Kicks"

While it’s been great to have a single venture as my focus, I’m starting to feel too slow about it. Focus is good, but it needs to be balanced with the ability to find something worth 100% of focus. Here I think I’ve had opportunity costs by focusing on one thing too early. 

I saw this recently on Instagram and it reminded me of how I had approached my ventures last year. Especially the “double your rate of failure” bit stuck with me. With one venture, I have a rate of 1. I could, and have in the past, parallelized 2 and 3 ventures. 

After all... I learned last year, after publishing 10 books, that – if I do everything else right – only 1 out of 10 will actually work and be profitable.

So, here’s a break-down of what I’m thinking:

Starting with the smallest unit, the experiment with its three steps, then sequencing that in one venture, then parallelizing multiple (non-cross-pollinating) ventures to double and triple my rate of failure.

However, this is pretty much an idea where everything always takes the same amount of time. In reality it looks more like this:

So, I do have my experiment board that allowed me to keep track of my experiments before. And I’m not crazy about the Evernote style so far… Should I just re-use my tracking system? Why did I stop using it?

See ⭐️ How To Make Better and Faster Investment-Decisions With Lean Experiments for details - 

Many questions today. But I’ll find the answer!

Key Benefits

MVP: "An Insights Development Environment (IDE), for you, forever."
Based on Obsidian Landing Page
"An Insights Development Environment (IDE)" 
 - Moderating interviews is such a good time to really meet someone on eye-level
 - We love connecting with people
 - Qualitative analysis is where the magic happens
 - Where you discover and develop insights from your interviews
 - Once the interviews are over and the transcripts have arrived, you hit a brick-wall. 
 - It's hard though without good tools
 - Your IDE should help you spend more quality time with your transcripts
 - In DeepDive, reading, coding, segmenting and analysing your interview transcripts is frictionless. 
 - Take a first pass of coding with alias-coding, 
 - review and dive deeper, 
 - highlight quotes with a single keyboard stroke, 
 - develop your coding book, 
 - pepper in your segments and 
 - marvel at what patterns emerge 

"For you"
 - Coding interview transcripts is incredibly personal. 
 - You want to connect with your interview partners after you've spoken with them
 - You want to also move fast and get into flow quickly
 - You also want to keep your transcripts secure
 - And you want to deliver your report ahead of time for fine-tuning with your team
 - DeepDive is... 
 - Native Mac application
 - it's much faster than any web-based application
 - It hooks into your computer directly
 - It's built to be 100% Customizable 
 - 26 Hotkeys that you can assign to your codes for speed-of-thought coding
 - 5 coding color schemes to make it easy to parse at a glance
 - Limitless coding books per project so you can fine-tune your insights
 - Limitless segmenting of your interviews so you can slice and dice during analysis
 - Built-in "Auto-Coding" that automatically tags 
 - AI-Coding – Your DeepDive has a local AI engine built-in that learns as you code your transcripts and over time matures to the point of assisting you

"Forever"
 - "In our age when cloud services can shut down, get bought, or change privacy policy any day, the last thing you want is proprietary formats and data lock-in."
 - With DeepDive, your data is stored locally and will not ever be held hostage by a cloud-provider 
 - Export your coded transcripts anytime to fully portable Excel or CSV
 - CSV export also gives you the unparalleled interoperability to use any kind of sync, encryption, or data processing that works with plain text files.

id: ⭐️ Pageturner Hack for Kindle – Experiment (W21 Mini-Project).md
text:
TLDR; After getting frustrated, angry even, with how awkward and unreliable the "touch-screen-to-flipt-to-next-page" on the Kindle Classic is, I experimented with different ways to emulate a physical 'next-page' button akin to those found on more expensive devices like the Kindle Oasis. My ideal solution turned out to be a simple, twisted rubber band.

Demo

Meta-Learning
The solution is much simpler and less complex (a fucking twisted rubber band!?) than I had expected – "Less But Better"
What seems obvious and laughable now I was only able to discover through the process of iteration, experimentation and elimination

🔥 The problem I'm solving for

The issue is that paging next with the regular Kindle is really, really AWKWARD and UNRELIABLE
Turning/flipping to the next page BREAKS MY READING FLOW because...
 - I have to LIFT my thumb from its resting position 😒
 - I have to MOVE my thumb above the screen 😞
 - I have to PRESS my thumb HARD onto the screen 😔
 - Then ONLY HALF (50%) of presses don't register 🔥🤬🔥
 - So half the time I have to press again (WTF?) 🔥🔥🔥🔥🤬🔥🔥🔥🔥
 - I have to LIFT my thumb again 😔
 - I have to MOVE my thumb back to its resting position 😞

What I want
I just want effortless and reliable page turns with my current Kindle
Looking at the much higher-priced model, like the Oasis, there are physical buttons for navigation to the next and previous page but that costs north of 250€. 250€ for effortless page turns? 🤨

My ideal solution
Ideally my current Kindle had ONE button for NEXT PAGE 🙂
Ideally that button was located where my thumb naturally RESTS 😍
Ideally that button took practically NO EFFORT to press 🤩
Ideally that button was RELIABLE to trigger the page turn more than 80% of the time 😍

My current minimum viable solution

A simple rubber band (4mm width)
Placed perfectly flush to the outer border of screen
With an intentional TWIST 

Features
Thumb can rest 
Motion to trigger page turn is effortless
 - Only 2mm horizontal motion
 - No vertical motion required
The twist in the band is more reliable 
 - 90% of presses are registered
The twist in the band makes it 'clicky', more tangible

Experiments – How I got here (The long story) 
Resources
My Kindle as the "test-bed"
A collection of materials that seemed reasonable to use

Iteration 1 – Using a clamp, paperclip and capacitative rubber nib

Riskiest Assumption
Having a button device thingy makes the reading experience BETTER by increasing flow by decreasing friction while turning pages

Learnings
No material except the rubber tip of the "tablet pen" triggered page-flip efficiently
Overall using the nib as shown above, this worked really welle
This worked far better than it looks
The tension on the paperclip wire even made a clicking sound when pressed (Nice)
Being able to REST my thumb is crucial to entering a state of reading flow
Minimizing the EFFORT to turn the page is also crucial to entering a state of reading flow

Result
I read a whole evening with it and enjoyed it 
Definitely BETTER THAN WITHOUT
Less effort/friction during page-flips
Increased reading flow

Questions
Q: What kind of rubber are on those pen tips?
A: "Conductive elastomer"[^1]

Decision
Persevere/Keep with the overall "pageturner" idea
Pivot/Change on attachment and mechanics

Idea 2 – Using a rubber band for attaching the capacitative nib

Couldn't find a good way to attach the cut-up nib to the rubber band
Overall, this approach further reduced the effort to press

Learnings, Result, Questions, and Decision
Rubber band much easier to attach
Doesn't SCRATCH the surface
Even less effort to turn page
What if the capacitative nib isn't even needed?
Perservere/Keep rubber band
Pivot/Change trigger nib

Iteration 3 – Using the rubber band straight-up without extra nib

Riskiest Assumption
Using the rubber band directly has enough effective capacity to trigger page-flips

Method

Learnings
When stretched along the device, there is the perfect gap between rubber and screen
It's slightly harder to rest thumb because it's right above the screen (To avoid accidental flips)

Result
Regular rubber CAN effectively trigger page-flip (at 70% reliability)

Decision
Persevere/Keep: Single rubber band
Pivot/Change: Improve trigger efficiency towards 80-100%

Iteration 4 – Adding a TWIST for efficiency

Riskiest Assumption
Adding a TWIST to the rubber band increases the RELIABILITY 

Method
Add the TWIST and sample 20+ page turns in a realistic setting

Result
85% Efficiency – 17/20 presses triggered a page-turn

Decision
Persevere/Keep: Twist
Pivot/Change: Increase efficiency/reliability further

Learnings
This allows to rest the thumb on the side while needing minimal effort to "toggle" the TWIST
Toggling the TWIST creates a pleasing haptic 'clicking' sensation similar to a button
The thumb-motion is not a top-down press anymore but a left-right swipe (Takes some time to get used to)

Iteration 5 – Experimenting with different TWISTS (1,2,3,4,5)

Riskiest Assumption
There is a way to twist the rubber band that increases RELIABILITY to 90% and improves on handling

Method
Try different levels of twist and see if that creates a better "UI" for my thumb

Learnings

Three Distinct Variables Affect Reliability
Playing with the different twists helped me realize that there are really 3 important variables that, taken together, effect how effortless and reliable the page is turned. 
When these three variables are in harmony so to speak, I've achieved 90+% reliablity of page turn registered while reading today
They're all very personal and depend on how you like to hold your Kindle, how big your hands are and how small the individual "twist-segments" are on the band.
Hence, there is no one-size-fits-all version of twists that work for everyone.

Variable 1: "Thumb Resting Sweet Spot" (50%)
This is where you place your thumb most of the time and relax it inbetween page turns. In terms of importance, to me, everything else in terms of usability derives from this. In my case, it's in the upper-half of the lowest third of the sidebar because of how I hold the Kindle. 

Variable 2: "Thumb Size" (25%)
This of course heavily depends on your individual thumb. Its size is in direct relation to how many twists your band can have. Once there are too many twists (max 5 for me), the segments become too small.

Variable 3: "Twist Segment Hot Spot Size" (25%)
This is how much vertical space each twist segment provides to register the touch/swipe motion. With each twist, the segments get smaller. For me 5 twists were the maximum. I learned that only the the flat middle-part works reliably when pressed.

Result
I have achieved 90+% RELIABLE PAGE TURNS once I harmonized my personal...
 - "Thumb Resting Sweet Spot" - Upper half of the bottom third
 - "Thumb Size" - Small
 - "Twist Segment Hot Spot Size" - 4 Twists, 3 Segments at 4cm each

Decision
Persevere/Keep: 4 Twists
Pivot/Change: Nothing, keep things as-is. I think this venture-hack has reached more than 90% reliability.

[^1]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conductiveelastomer, https://www.amazon.de/-/en/MobiLinyi-pieces-replacement-premium-stylus-6-mm/dp/B0797Y7M24/

id: ⭐️ My Light-Therapy Lamp Solution with Kindle.md
text:
A follow up on ⭐️ Happier Through Bright Light (Experiment)
My original Beurer SAD lamp broke while moving
I'm 100% convinced that light therapy works wonders for me
Winter in Berlin is here ❄️
I recently bought a new lamp (Beurer TL 30) with what seemed a better overall form-factor
Hoping that the new design would make it easier to sit still, have the lamp 10cm close by my face for 20 minutes

The lamp

The new design disappointed
After only 3 uses it was clear to me that this new device is NOT based on any real user research:
The new form-factor has NOT, at all, addressed the core design-issues that come up if you actually want to use it for 20 minutes at 10-20cm distance for the advertised 10,000 LUX
The green kick-stand is utterly useless if you actually want to use it for 20 minutes at 10-20cm distance for the advertised 10,000 LUX
The extra buldge on the backside to slide in the kick-stand is utterly annoying if you actually want to use it for 20 minutes at 10-20cm distance for the advertised 10,000 LUX
Holding the light with your hands close to your face for 20 minutes is also STILL utterly TEDIOUS if you actually want to use it for 20 minutes at 10-20cm distance for the advertised 10,000 LUX
The socket for the power-plug is also on the wrong side (the bottom) if you actually want to use it for 20 minutes at 10-20cm distance for the advertised 10,000 LUX
The cable is at least 1m too short if you actually want to use it for 20 minutes at 10-20cm distance for the advertised 10,000 LUX

In short, the new Beurer design is mostly a face-lift
The kick-stand more of an insult to actual users than an improvement
It's a disappointment because:
 - I can attest to the underlying method of action
 - Light therapy WORKS reliably when done early in the morning 
 - So the need for these devices is there
 - And the technology is finally small enough to pack 10,000 LUX in an A5-sized package
 - Which makes the resulting device perform even worse:
 - All the company (and the competitors in the market) can come up with is...
 - an plastic LED rectangle 
 - with a useless kick-stand
 - no way to hold it comfortably close to your face to 
 - and the power socket in the wrong place
 - And let's not get into how you still need to be connected to an electrical outlet, which, in itself seems like the grandest failure, especially since the cable that comes with the device is at least 1m too short to actually be useful

It makes me wonder...
 - WHO THE FUCK "designs" these things and GETS PAID for it?
 - It's clear that they have they never used it regulary themselves as recommended in the manual (20 minutes at 10cm distance for 10,000 Lux)
 - WHO THE FUCK came up with the shitty kick-stand that only works if you have it next to you while working 
 - which in turn means you have to have the lamp on for HOURS to get the benefit
 - which in turn is unacceptable and such design flaw and false fucking advertising in itself
 - Please fir.. ahem, reassign the product owner, the product manager and designer responsible for this to "a nice quiet farm upstate" where they can no longer build things that don't work because they clearly never took the time to talk to actual users or try it themselves for more than A HOT FUCKING MINUTE

The quest continued
So, as it's become clear to me that the producers of what essentially amounts to a plastic box with an 450-460nm wavelength LED array and a power cable DO NOT do THEIR HOMEWORK
So I have to, again, figure it out myself
What's the best setup and REASON to have this 10,000 LUX lamp 10cm close to your face that is bearable for about 20 minutes?
I really don't want to have to SIT STILL for 20 minutes doing NOTHING in the morning to gain the benefits

My solution
I came up with combining my Kindle and the light with duct-tape
S that I now can...
Spend the 20 minutes READING, aka acutally doing something USEFUL with some of my most valuable morning time
While, simultaneously having the SAD lamp very close to my face for gaining the actual THERAPEUTIC BENEFIT that I paid money for
And, for the necessary COMFORT of holding the lamp so close I've experimented with POP-SOCKETS and came to their optimal positioning

The ideal solution
The duct-tape version is 85% of my ideal solution
To make it 100% I would make the following changes:
 - 1. Make the light the same size as the Kindle
 - 2. Make the light battery-powered
 - 3. Have both, light and kindle slide into a simple cover
 - 4. IMPORTANT: Lastly, keep the POP-SOCKETS on both sides at the exact locations I had them

Details

To Beurer
For the inevitable person at Beurer who will see this and think...
 - "Hey, this is a great idea. We should build a light-therapy lamp that you use while you're reading on your eBook reader. 
 - "This actually makes the lamp usable and useful. Like a cover or something that connects the two devices neatly."
 - "And he's so right - We need something like the Pop-Sockets so you can actually hold it."
 - "Oh, and we'll just say 'we listened to our users' and spin it as some 'co-creation' design story. That'll make marketing super happy."
 - "And anyways, it's sooo obvious of a solution when you look at it... so instead of reaching out to the author for their fair 10% of profit-share per unit sold, it should ME who gets paid an extra bonus for it for finding it. I deserve that."
Listen up motherfucker
I'm tired of your bullshit 
You've had the chance to do your homework and do ACTUAL user research
And I'm not talking about that one time doing one of those tired, old, lip-service "customer-centric innovation" workshops that went no-fucking-where
You arriving here means you didn't do your work
I did your work 
I did the leg-work you should have done
...And I know, building plastic frames with LEDs is work
...And getting them certified for the German market as well...
Bla bla bla... 
I don't care
The short of it is: 
 - If you want to sell this
 - Then start by calculating in my 10% of profit-share per unit sold
 - And then contacting me with the right paper-work
A word of advice: Don't fuck this up

id: ⭐️ Kinesiotape for Psychological Well-Being – Experiment (S21 Mini-Project).md
text:
Background
Taping – as prescribed by my orthopedic doctor – works very well, much better than I had expected
I've recovered my achilles tendon within two weeks of wearing tape after struggling with sharp pain for almost a month
The consistent presence from the tape redirected my attention to my heel several times a day
I believe that consistently repeated, daily attention to a part of my body helped it physically heal faster

I've also learned that...
When giving myself space and time to connect with myself, either through therapy or daily me-time, I noticed that certain psychological pains also have specific places in my body
For example, sadness (unsurprisingly) manifests as a sharp pain around my physical heart

What if...
What if you could use kinesio-tape to help support healing psychological pain as well?
 - By stimulating the physical area where it manifests
 - By consistently directing my attention to that part of my body

Prototype for sadness

For supporting sadness, disappointment and grief.
Emotions that have been very difficult for me to allow and process.
Hypothesis: I believe that if I tape above my physical (and emotional) heart, then I will direct my attention to my heart and its emotions more often...
 - ... which I believe will result in giving emotions, including the difficult ones for me - such as sadness - more attention and Safe SpaceSafe Space to heal and prosper

Tracking
Day 1: The tape is soft and nice to wear. I've found myself being reminded to mentally "look there" 5 times in 12 hours.
title: Kinesiotape for Psychological Well-Being – Experiment (S21 Mini-Project)

text:
My motherJoyce Rondeau, Mother died after a long and courageous battle with cancer.

It felt like watching a deadly car-crash in slow-motion. Stretched out over ten agonising, depressing, and feeling-out-of-control years.

I last saw my mother around the 31st of December 2016 when I finished visiting my parents in Spain. She had been very weak and in pain and needed to lay down more then usual. The years of chemo and pain-medication had taken its toll on her body and her spirit. Her mind was still clear and she spoke about money, her brother and me.

I remember the last time I saw her, after we had said good-bye, passing by her window as she lay back into bed. I did not know this was the last time. I figured, after 10 years of ups and downs, this would be another one.

We spoke on the phone a few days later and she sounded very tired and out of it. I still didn't make much of it, I wasn't worried more than usual. We spoke one more time when I told her about a cold I had gotten. I remember she wished me well.

Two weeks into January, my fatherHeinz Rondeau called me and told me they had to move her to the hospital. She had been too weak to stand up. And that he couldn't take care of her anymore because he, too, was now too weak. He sounded heavy so I started to worry, too. I asked him if I could talk with her but he said she was too weak at the moment. I should try again in a few days.

I asked him if I should fly down to Spain but he refused: "There's nothing you can do right now." Then another week passed, he said she had a few good days but slid in and out of consciousness. That's the first time we decided I was on "stand-by" to fly down.

In the late afternoon of the 5th of February, I got "the phone call". The call I had dreaded for ten years since My mothers cancer diagnosis 2008. That ONE call in which my dad asked me to buy a ticket and come as soon as I can to see my mother, who was still alive, one last time.

I bought the ticket to fly out of Tegel early next morning to arrive at the hospital before 11am. I remember taking a Taxi to the airport at 6am. Then getting on the airplane feeling still and numb and yet completely functional. Two hours later, at around 9am, I landed in Palma de MallorcaMallorca, Spain. I switched on my phone and received my fathers WhatsApp message. My mother had passed away over night. And that I needed to come to say good-bye as soon as possible due to hospital regulations.

I took another Taxi and arrived at about 10 or 10:30. I first saw my father who explained to me what happened. She had not been conscious for most of the past days. Had been on pain-management. Her breathing had slowed down last night. He stayed with her for the whole night. Singing her her favourite song "San Francisco" by Scott McKenzie over and over as she passed away.

I had twenty minutes to say good-bye before the hospital had to move her to the morgue.

I entered the room. To the right her hospital bed appeared. I moved closer and saw her body. Eyes closed, her thin hands folded, still.
title: My mothers death in 2018

text:
While it’s been great to have a single venture as my focus, I’m starting to feel too slow about it. Focus is good, but it needs to be balanced with the ability to find something worth 100% of focus. Here I think I’ve had opportunity costs by focusing on one thing too early. 

I saw this recently on Instagram and it reminded me of how I had approached my ventures last year. Especially the “double your rate of failure” bit stuck with me. With one venture, I have a rate of 1. I could, and have in the past, parallelized 2 and 3 ventures. 

After all... I learned last year, after publishing 10 books, that – if I do everything else right – only 1 out of 10 will actually work and be profitable.

So, here’s a break-down of what I’m thinking:

Starting with the smallest unit, the experiment with its three steps, then sequencing that in one venture, then parallelizing multiple (non-cross-pollinating) ventures to double and triple my rate of failure.

However, this is pretty much an idea where everything always takes the same amount of time. In reality it looks more like this:

So, I do have my experiment board that allowed me to keep track of my experiments before. And I’m not crazy about the Evernote style so far… Should I just re-use my tracking system? Why did I stop using it?

See ✨ How To Make Better and Faster Investment-Decisions With Lean Experiments for details - 

Many questions today. But I’ll find the answer!

id: ⭐️ How To Make Better and Faster Investment-Decisions With Lean Experiments.md
text:
As many of you know by now, I strongly believe in the effectiveness of using the scientific method to validate business ideas.

Earlier this year, I began running a bunch of experiments for my ideas and ventures. But, quickly, my experiments became too much to handle on a white-board with stickies. I switched to a Google Sheet but that didn't have the usability and speed that I loved from using stickies.

So I decided to build a simple experiment tracking system for myself.

Keeping Track of Ventures, Experiments and Costs

I would say it's pretty basic and covers exactly what I need to keep track of:

My Ventures which are a sequential list of experiments and their Pivot-or-Persevere decision. Ventures can also be aborted if there is no encouraging signal.
Experiments, which comprise of:
 - Theory
 - Riskiest Assumption
 - Method
 - Prediction
 - Outcome
 - Decision
 - Cost
 - Learnings
Cost tracking
 - Per Experiment
 - Per Venture
 - Overall

I added software once I maxed out on paper
Note that I built the tracking software only once I had run out of space on my physical custom-madeExperiment Board 2.0 Lean Experiment Board

Types Of Experiments:

I templated the main three experiment types that I usually run:

Market Experiment
Market Experiment – Usually an overview how big the market is, how much traffic there is, how the market has grown so far.

Customer/Problem Experiment

Customer/Problem Experiment – If the market is attractive, I ask myself, what problems do these people really have? Depending on my theory and riskiest assumption I might do interviews or keyword research or – something I've fallen in love with – analyze Amazon customer reviews.

Problem/Solution Experiment

Problem/Solution Experiment – Knowing the problem, can I come up with a solution that is attractive to the customer segment?

Sales-Funnel Experiments
Once I have nailed those three, I start running custom experiments for Acquisition, Activation, Retention and Revenue (but not earlier.)

If you look at my dashboard below, I've run 43 Experiments for 14 Ventures. As you'll see, based on my learnings I aborted more than 2/3rds of my Ventures and continued on only a few promising ones.

I think that's been a huge value for me. To know and to be sure when to persevere and when not.

So far, I'm quiet happy with it. It's rudimentary but works.

And since the Venture Board was, in itself, an experiment for myself (My theory was that I'll consistently use it to track my progress and costs) –

I'm persevering.

Let me know if you would like early-bird access to the board. Simply comment below.

Thanks for reading!

Lean Experiment Board
Lean Experiment Board 2.0.pdf
title: How To Make Better and Faster Investment-Decisions With Lean Experiments

While on vacation at my Dad's, I bought a tiny note-pad and pen and started carrying it around with me everywhere. I use it to Read to Feed and How to hunt for ideas like an artist.

This tiny notebook has since become a gamechanger for me to quicky capture notes and drawings that I would have otherwise "lost". I still find that my phone is one of the worst ways to capture ideas quickly and with focus. 

Because it's so small, I've taken my notebook on practically every walk I've gone on. While I'm walking, when an idea comes up or I read or see something cool, I whip it out, take the pen and write. 

The time from "oh, let me note this" to pen-on-paper is less than 3 seconds with this setup. To me, this speed and the flexibility that paper offers (write, draw, illustrate, etc.) is ideal.

text:
Background

I’m not 100% sure how I will take my dream about doing this and make it happen. Today I feel very tired and less motivated. I enjoy dreaming about it and I enjoy imagining the benefits of it but I’m not yet ready to start the work. Or at least I’m pushing that away. Yesterday I spent most of the time fantasizing and then 1 hour actually planning this challenge. 

And maybe that’s okay right now. Maybe I need to give myself time to get into it. Maybe I need to clarify the vision for this challenge and get really excited about it BEFORE I start planning all the details and todos. 

Good question. How do I envision this process? How do I envision this project? I know there’s an outcome, at least for now, with 300 In-Depth Interviews Challenge… So that’s good but not really exciting. 100 beans. 100 cups. 100 people. 300 In-Depth Interviews Challenge. Doesn’t say anything. 100 problems captured. 100 ideas generated. 100 business ideas. 100 problems to solve to make money. 100 opportunities to empathize and be creative about something someone cares about.

How I want this experience - The “HOW” to the “WHAT”

I want to experience my ‘ONE Thing’ in work. I want to focus and know and feel absolutely right. I want to work on it every day and see progress and results and changes and improvements. I want to become an expert in listening. I want to become an expert in generating ideas. I want to create what Dane M. created but even better and bigger and more exciting. I want to be the person that people think of when they think of profitable business ideas. I want to be desired and asked to help and asked to join teams in amazing companies. I want to start and focus on the most important part in work, the problem and pain that people face and figure out ways to solve those in exchange for money. I want to connect with those I interview. I want to make them feel special. I want them to feel safe and cared for. I want them to unlock their potential and creativity safely and with joy. I want others to see that process and begin themselves. I want to share the interviews and help business owners build better products that actually help people. I want to OWN this part. I want to unearth, discover the gems that are hidden. I want to bring those gems to the surface. I want to help 100 people solve their biggest pain in business and life. I want to feel success in conducting these interviews. I want to talk to amazing people. I want to connect with amazing people. I want to build a portfolio site and channel and following that is the foundation for my work. I want to start at the core source of energy and drive incredibly successful business from it. I want to help and co-uncover ideas that are so simple and so clear that it’s completely obvious and doable to build a solution and make money immediately. I want to be sought after and courted by companies and venture firms and start ups and businesses to help them unearth gems. I want to experience work as a joyful and incredibly fun experience that uplifts me and those I am in connection with. I want to experience connection and joy and fun as part of work. I want to build a new life for myself that works for me and that feels right and good. I want this to be my project, my focus, my source of motivation. I want to feel excited and amped up and curious and surprised and connected and referred to and I want to publish and spread and impress and have a portfolio and content and a clear stance. 

I see myself contacting amazing people and getting their yes and sending them the invite and starting the session and recording the session and kicking off the conversation and feeling great and focused and connected and asking and listening and taking notes and reflecting and probing and making them feel good and confident and creative and digging a little more and being careful and respectful and finding an idea and polishing that idea and getting excitement and feeling relief and feeling a sense of liberation and clarity and gratitude and recapping and finding an actual price and feeling good about it. And then slowly finishing off and getting a referral to the next IDEAL interview partner and hearing that they’d love to talk another round because they got so much out of it this time. 

And I see myself finishing the zoom call and feeling really good and excited and inspired and I see myself taking a few more notes and organizing the note and the follow-up and the referral and the recording. I see myself editing the recording and uploading it and getting the transcript for it and publishing it on my site and on Facebook and on Instagram and LinkedIn and getting amazing responses and feeling an immense sense of success. I see myself adding one more interview to my list and looking forward to the next one. 

Reflection

Yes, this feels much better. Much more in tune with actually doing it. This feels like I’m already doing it. This makes so much sense. I believe that focusing on the feeling and the experience as I want to have it is good. I’m definitely more amped up than I was an hour ago. 

Having a vision of “HOW” is super important. The “WHAT” has been clear (300 In-Depth Interviews Challenge) for a few days and I can get excited about that as a challenge but it’s also important to get emotional about it to have the energy and the vibe and the creativity that’s needed to make it happen.

I’ve also done the “Why do I want this?” and “Why do I believe I will get this?” and I guess the “How do I want this?” is another part in this process to give it color and dimension and emotions.

I’ll let this sink in for a little bit and then decide on what’s next in this process.

Now for a little break.

text:
Did a Retrospective 3.7.2020
Sent out the complete LifeScan Phase Two Interviews – First Impressions as PDF to my team...
Still got to edit my own rent contract 
Print it out
Buy stuff for tomorrow:
 - Fennel Salad #done
 - Fennel 
 - Lemons
 - Parmigiano
 - Burger buns 3 x 6 #done
 - Iceberg Salad x 1 #done 
 - Tomatos x 1 #done
 - Once I get there:
 - Ice cubes
 - 2 x six-packs of american beers

Learned a little more about Obsidian, enabled the daily note plugin since I've been creating a daily note already by hand most days. Got the $25/life license to get beta builds (worth it already because backlinks were broken and CPU used 100% by the graph renderer.)

Talked to Jonathan Najarian on the phone for a bit; we did a quick check-in because he was headed to a gig and I had to go buy stuff. Printed out the rent contracts before. What else? Got all the stuff for the grilling tomorrow. I'm not sure if I want to head back to What I love about Franziska Krüger tonight after 10pm. I kind of feel like spending some time with myself. A lot has happened this week and I'm exhausted. I spent a lot of Money. I didn't make that much Money in return... But in the idea of expanding, I feel good about spending money on myself for myself. And most of it was Food-related anyway, which I think is good and worth it. 

I'm good sitting around right now. Maybe watch Notes on Dane Maxwell's video about Pick a Niche Article later.

Read the article, overall good, just not feeling particularly marketing-y or sales-y right now. I just want to chill and maybe eat something later and then go to bed and start the weekend tomorrow.

Woke up tired, got out of bed at 9. Feeling like shit. Feeling exhausted and incredibly sad. Sat on the couch yesterday all day. No Dopamine-hits, no scrolling etc. I think that’s the right decision. Same today. I have two interviews. The one I did yesterday was the highlight of my day. Other than that, I didn’t do much. I went shopping and cooked chicken. That was good. 

For right now I’m glad I went out for a walk through the park. I wish I could cry it all out. I wish I could cry so that this pain and suffering has a place to be. I looked at that tree that reminds me of me. It has a vine plant creeping up and someone other than me cut that vine. And now there’s a skeleton left of that vine and the tree is growing much better now than last year. I identify with the tree and hope I am in the process of cutting my vine off. 

I feel slow and sad and heavy. At least allergies are back to a manageable level. This month sucked ass. It was basically 4 weeks of not sleeping because of allergies, becoming aware of how bad my early “work”-experience was and that I’m a survivor. No one really cares even if I tell them. I have to pay too much money that I don’t have. I feel small and hurt and sad and alone and broke and broken. 

Maybe that’s why I’ve been Broke so much. I’m just a nobody with nothing of value. I’m just someone you pass on the street, a somebody who serves you dinner. My life has no meaning anymore. Twenty years of living a lie, lying to myself just to survive. That’s what they call a survivor. I haven’t thrived once in the last Twenty years. I’ve been on the edge of failure, ruin, heart-break and death and I managed to never fall off the rails. No wonder I smoked like a chimney. No wonder. 

It wasn’t my fault but it still happened to me. 

And now I know why nothing ever worked out for me in the last fucking Twenty years. At least I know now. Getting glasses when you’re short-sighted is great because you start seeing the world clearly. It also shows you the stuff that’s wrong and broken or where you suffered. Clarity sheds a light on everything, the good, the bad and the ugly truths. And so, finally, I’ve been in a position to look at the ugly truths in my life. And the ugly people in my life that made my time miserable and maimed me for the rest of my life. What happened was not okay. It was not appropriate. It was completely inappropriate and wrong. It was wrong. 

So, for today, what’s my plan? 

 Interview #2 with Dr. Moaz [DONE]
 ???
 Interview #3 with Annika [DONE]
 ???
 ???
 ???
 Call with JN at 6pm: Interview
 Head over to What I love about Franziska Krüger’s at 7pm for dinner
 Get an overview of current finances/expenses

I don’t know yet what comes after the interviews. Gotta make sure I write down my first impressions again. That seemed to be valuable to me and the client. 

Worrying about money. 40 and Broke. 40 and Broke. 40 and broken. 40 and worthless. 40 and nobody. 40 and survived. 40 and… ?

Dopamine Fast Day 2

I’m supposed to focus on what I want. I want to focus on what I want. But it’s hard today. It’s hard when you’re depressed. 

I should keep moving more. 

 I will not check my phone.
 I will not go on social media.
 I will not read news.
 I will not eat sugar.
 I will not eat fast food. 
 I will not watch porn. 

I will not get high on bullshit, low-value, high-dopamine hits to avoid difficult feelings anymore. I’m doing this for ME. Instead, I’ll do stuff that’s good for me and that will feel good when I don’t baseline myself with those drugs! 

And I was successful there yesterday. No random dopamine hits throughout the day. 

No mindless scrolling to ease the pain. 

No coffee or nicotine! (Non-smoker for over 4 months now!)

Instead, 

 I will move my body
 I will eat good food
 I will read good books
 I will exercise my body
 I will meditate
 I will allow difficult emotions
 I will allow difficult conversations
 I will write 

And I don’t need to stress out that I’m not yet the productivity-machine reading 3 books every day on day 2 of my dopamine fast. If I can avoid the brain-sugar bullshit, all other productive things will come back one by one. 

Maybe I’ve been so hooked on that shit is because my trauma was so big as well. Where others just dipped their toes once in a while, I was fully invested because it gave me relief from my pain. 

Interview #2 Preparations

Anyways, the interview is coming up in 25 minutes. I don’t have much more coherent thinking available at the moment. And that’s okay. Just kept writing and got some ideas out of it. I wonder how air conditioning works in the new place on Alexanderplatz Apartment?

Still got 5 minutes left on my tomato timer. What else can I write about that’s relevant and interesting? 

How I want to feel

I want to wake up in the morning full of energy and feel tirelessly motivated to live my own life. To work on something that fulfills me and that lets me enjoy success and financial independence. To have a loving relationship with my partner and my family and my friends. To be free of worry about money. To choose experiences because I want them, being certain that all resources like money will be available to me. To be full of energy and focused. To be alert and “there” and flow effortlessly through my day from one activity to the next to a different place, in and out of conversations etc. Free of feeling hurt and sadness. Full of positive, hopeful, optimistic feelings.

After Interview with Dr. Moaz

Super nice, learned a lot. Had fun. I think she enjoyed it as well. Good intuitions on what she said. Good training for my own interviews. Good probing, good memory on what was said. Good notes. Good first impressions. Overall a success! Time flew by, I asked mostly open-ended questions. 

Now, I have one hours to spend before the next call. That’ll be at 1:30, then I’ll have a longer break until talking to Jonathan Najarian at 6pm. Feels crazy that the day is already that far ahead. But I slept in until 9am, so… 

Idea Regarding “Interviews” 

“Start with ONE” - Marketing course that starts with ONE customer that gets interviewed for problems and solutions. Find a really painful problem, then come up with solutions until a paid solution is found and that pain is solved. 

1. One Person that I like spending time with
2. One Problem that they seriously struggle with
3. One Solution that they’ll pay for

Use interview to come up with a “Person(a)” like Jonathan Najarian, 30 years old, lives in Boston, works with his girlfriend as wedding-photographer, 2-person team, city-wide booking. Could even be a friend, because it’s about their problem and their solution and not some random idea I’ve come up with. Maybe. This needs to be seen. 

Use interview to capture emotionally charged problem description “XYZ fucking sucks, man. If this doesn’t go away, things’ll get fucking ugly.” This can be used directly in sales copy for this one particular person. A sales-letter for ONE that basically recaps the conversation and the idea/offer that was created together. 

Use interview to create product/idea/offer in a way that it’s valuable to them and they’re ready to pay for it. Using quotes and the feature-list, build a landing-page (could be email) to presell the service.

BOOM!

Deliver the service as discussed and promised and paid for. Ask for feedback, improvements. 

Get testimonial, referrals and introductions. 

Scale business system slowly.

 “We’re all just walking each other home.” – Ram Dass

Thought: Would any of these notes I’ve been writing be worth/useful to others? 

Just thought, I could publish this on a site so that at least What I love about Franziska Krüger and my dad would have an idea of where I’m at… 

Where is freeisaverb.com hosted actually? 

Requested account deletion on HostGator, BlueHost, Medium, Twitter

Should make my LinkedIn profile private!

Should probably cancel Clickfunnels…

Uff, ja, also heute ging’s nochmal richtig um’s Eingemachte. Und ich bin froh, dass ich gerade die Zeit und den Kopf dafür habe. Ich kann mich relativ fokussiert daran setzen und da irgendwie durch arbeiten. Es muss raus. Es geht hier um MEIN LEBEN. Und erst jetzt, mit Medikament, kann ich erst damit wirklich umgehen. Was ein Glück, dass ich das für mich entdeckt habe. Schreiben scheint ein guter Weg zu sein, das zu verarbeiten. Ich weiss nicht, was da gerade noch besser wäre, aber ich fühle mich wohl hier am Keyboard, in Ruhe. Ich hatte mir gewünscht, dass ich irgendwie schon weiter bin in meinem Leben. Dass ich mich total auf Jobsuche und Beziehung und Wohnung und Spass und Freunde und Berlin konzentrieren kann. Aber ich bin da einfach nicht. Und ich werde da auch erst dann sein, wenn ich das hier heile. Und ich bin so froh, dass mit der Hilfe von Psilocybin und Ritalin ich das Problem erkenne und es aktiv lösen kann, weil ich mich fokussieren kann. Alles, war in meinem Leben in den letzten 20 Jahren los war, war in direktem Bezug auf das Traumatic Experience at Work, das ich momentan bespreche. Es ist irrsinnig krass, was damals passiert ist, wie rücksichtslos mit mir umgegangen wurde. Wie krass, dass es den Tätern nur um Macht und Geld ging und ich die Geschichte vom Weltverbessern geglaubt habe. 

Ohne da jetzt wieder einzusteigen: Ich sollte nach dieser Runde etwas leckeres Essen, eine Pause machen und mich auf das konzentrieren, was ich will. Das tut mir wirklich gut und es macht Sinn und wenn ich mich mit dem Scheiss beschäftigen muss, dann ist es immer in Beziehung zu meinem besseren Leben in meiner nahen Zukunft! Diesen Fokus auf die guten Dinge zu halten ist jetzt noch viel wichtiger als jemals zuvor! Denn so kann ich mein Leben zurückgewinnen und meine Stabilität und meinen Selbstwert. Ich bin stolz darauf, hier und jetzt genau diese Arbeit zu machen. Ich bin stolz darauf, denn ich stehe hier und jetzt für mich und mein Leben ein und setze Grenzen und schaffe mir meine Zukunft in der es mir gut geht, in der ich aufblühe, in der ich und mein Leben und meine Arbeit und mein Geld und meine Beziehungen gedeihen. Genau so wie damals, 1999 in New York, und noch viel besser! Und darum geht es. Es geht um mich. Es geht um meine Bedürfnisse. Es geht um mein Leben. Um meine Zeit. Dass es mir wieder gut geht. Dass ich mein Leben lebe. Ich bin stolz, dass ich es bis hier her geschafft habe. Dass ich nicht aufgegeben habe. Dass ich mich nicht umgebracht habe. Dass ich andere so gut es ging vor diesem Problem geschützt habe. Dass ich an mir selbst gearbeitet habe. Dass ich mir selbst zugehört habe, dass ich meinem inneren Klang gefolgt bin auch wenn es schwer war. Dass ich mir selbst Stufen in den Stein gehauen habe um aus dem Loch herauszukommen. Ich finde, ich mache das sehr, sehr gut. Ich finde, dass ich jetzt schon, im Verarbeiten und Heilen dieses Themas einen Riesen Erfolg schaffe. Ich fühle mich jetzt schon besser und größer und stärker und fokussierter als jemals in den letzten 20 Jahren!

Also, daher die abschliessenden Worte… 

Das ist die richtige Arbeit, die ich hier mache. Es ist die wichtige Arbeit, die mich dahin führt wo ich es mir wünsche. Es ist ganz schön harte Arbeit, aber ich habe sie gemacht. Es ist härter, nichts zu tun und sein Leben kaputt gehen zu sehen. Daher ist diese Arbeit und diese Zeit und diese Herausforderung die beste Investition in meine Zukunft. In meine Arbeit. In mein Vermächtnis. In den Spass und die Freude, die ich in meinem Leben erleben will. Dieses Thema, diese Befreiung ist die wichtigste Arbeit, die ich in meinem Leben jetzt verrichten kann. Und ich bin unglaublich dankbar, dass ich körperlich und geistig und seelisch dazu jetzt in der Lage bin. Und vielleicht kann ich irgendwann jemand Anderem helfen, sich so zu befreien.

AR
title: Post-Shadow Journal 09.06.2020

text:
Noch ein weiterer Eintrag für heute...

I did 2 hours of Deep Work – got the funnel ready and even found a good name for the overarching brand: MindSky Academy. Nice! Got the domain, that's verifying, but once it is, I'll finalize the Google Suite thing and then head over to mailerlite to verify my account with my fancy alexis@mindskyacademy.com email address. Pretty cool!

I'm happy it's the end of the week, I'm not that sharp anymore after working every day since Monday but I feel like I've pushed myself forward and kept good records of every amount of effort I put in. In total it's 14 hours of Deep Work (not counting work for C Space) working on my MindSky funnel and products and copy and videos. 14 hours I've invested in myself and my future and that worked. I need to eat more throughout the day, that was the only issue I haven't tackled yet. I'll try HUEL to make sure I eat something until I have the time to cook a meal. 

So yeah, I'm pretty stoked about this week! I bought myself flowers that I put on my desk and that makes it nice to sit here. They have a calming effect and are beautiful to look at. I think they're enjoying their stay. I hope. 

Since I cleaned up my desk last week and continued to remove anything that wasn't essential from it I like working here much more. It's the bare necessities I need to work and no distractions. The checklist above the table has also helped tremendously. I don't yet know how to ensure 100% that I start a timer before I go into work but it's working. I'm missing 20% maximum of sessions from my timer this week. That happens when I'm just in the zone I think. The little triangle stars I'm using to reward and celebrate are cute. I wish there were more of them. Or different stickers. And those that I don't know what it's going to be ahead of time (like a variable reward kind of thing) – I'll look into that next week. Maybe Modulor is open again or that toy store down the street. 

In either case, I feel like I'm developing, rapidly, a way for me to work hard and long and feel good about it. This is a major progress for me from staring into space or sleeping to working and getting things done consistently. I am proud that I've found a solution to my problem (Ritalin) and am excited to be ABLE to shape my life the way I want it to. 

YES!

Montag, 18.5.2020 – Irgendwie fühle ich mich seit Freitag komisch. Also auch schon davor, aber heute bin ich erst um 10:00 aus dem Bett gekommen. Irgendwas stört mich oder macht mich traurig. Ich glaube, es hat mit What I love about Franziska Krüger zu tun. Dem Streit von letztens. Und das hängt mir glaube ich noch nach. Also, den Elan von den letzten Wochen habe ich gerade nicht. Vielleicht bin ich auch enttäuscht, dass das mit dem OFAC Projekt doch nicht, gar nicht, hinhaut und ich da so viel Arbeit reingesteckt habe. Vielleicht auch das. Die Bewerbungen gehen eigentlich ganz gut. Aber heute schon mit Oleksii zu sprechen wegen einer Position geht mir etwas schnell. Also, wenn ich mich frage ob es mir gut geht muss ich sagen nein, ich fühle mich irgendwie off oder daneben. Sehr komisch. Könnte auch vom Essen letzte Woche kommen. Und dieser Fokus Mode hier geht auch irgendwie nicht so wie er sollte. Das der gesamte Text immer gehighlighted wird ist doch nicht die Idee, oder? 

Was gibt’s denn sonst so? Fühl mich müde und umfokussiert. Vielleicht hat das auch damit zu tun, dass ich am Samstag nicht dosiert hatte. Oder, dass ich jeden Tag dosier und das zu viel oder zu oft ist. Ich weiss es nicht. 

Zumindest habe ich für die Woche noch keine gute Vision. 

Also, irgendwie ist da der Wurm drin gerade. 

Erstmal habe ich schlechte Laune, bin frustriert, bin traurig. Fühle mich alleine. Fühle mich schwer. 

Das ist echt komisch weil es mir eigentlich gut geht! 

Ich hatte ein tolles Wochenende. Hab gut geschlafen. Hab hier gerade meine Ruhe… Also an sich passt doch alles. 

Was kann ich tun, damit ich mich irgendwie besser fühle? Welcher Gedanke macht da gerade für mich Sinn?

So. Today was a good day so far. I finally broke my own record of working 4h straight (with pauses every 30 minutes) on my Deep Work – specifically building my funnel following the OFAC framework. I'm proud because I still have time and energy to write about it now and I feel like I can do this again. I crossed the 4h mile! And yes, the Ritalin is definitely helping with this, especially in the moments where there's a distraction and I'm able to ignore it and re-focus. I also made myself a first draft of a checklist before getting to work. Here are the check-marks that have to be answered with 'yes' before I actually start the work:

Do I have...
1. A goal? 
2. Taken a break? 
3. A plan?
4. A good task? 
5. A reward? 
6. Removed distractions?
7. Water and snacks?
8. A timer set? 

So far, through 8 sessions of 30 minutes each (a longer pomodoro) I used the checklist to make sure I could fully focus on the task before me. 

One task, setting up the email integration, took much longer than expected because I wanted to use a service that doesn't cost anything (yet), works with CF and allows for automations in the free tier. It took me an hour of trying different services out until I settled on MailerLite with Zapier. It's a little hacky but it works as much as I need it to. The only thing missing is getting the MailerLite account verified for which I need a custom email address like alexis@mindsky.com – Which prompted me to (capture the need for) brainstorm a company name/product suite name. Something like MindSky is really nice... But that will have to wait until tomorrow, that's the next task at hand to finish up my email system: A verified MailerLite account. It'll cost $5 per month for the Google business suite which I wish I didn't have to pay for (didn't they have a free offer as well??)

Anyways, yes, pretty excited. Implemented the opt-in page, the responder (including a fresh account), the sequence of 5 emails, the 5 pages that belong to it. I'm so fucking glad to use PLR.me templates instead of having to come up with all of that on my own. For training purposes, this is really helpful. And I used FunnelScripts to write a good headline and sub-headline and the CTA for me. If anything, If I can really, truly stay to be the CONDUCTOR/COMPOSER focusing on the offers, the story and the hook and leave EVERYTHING else to someone or something else, would be tremendous. 

In other news, I got a mouse, a bluetooth one and I like it a lot. It does need a mouse pad on my table which is unfortunate but I think that would've been the case with any mouse I buy. Other than that it works really well! I haven't had a mouse in a decade I believe. But with my table/seat/keyboard set up this makes a lot of sense. Like right now, I'm using my external keyboard to type and if I need anything I can just lean right, grab my mouse instead of having to completely shift my body to reach OVER my keyboard and use my trackpad on my laptop. 

Oh, this reminds me, I still get to do my prosperity game today (and yesterday's) which means I have a lot of money (play-money for now) to "spend" on something I'd love. Like a enormous display and/or fully loaded iMac. Maybe that's the idea. The fully loaded iMac and a long trip to Paris. 

You know what? That's what I'm going to do now to make sure I've spent good time on it.

id: New Retrospective Format Highlights Blessings And Successes.md
text:
I’ve created an empowering and fun new Retrospective format for myself. I’ve enjoyed it tremendously.

I’ve found that the more I focus on the good that’s happening in my life, the better I feel.

I call the format "Highlights, Blessings and Successes.”

As you probably guessed it, you collect and appreciate exactly the things that went well.

Highlights – For me, that’s usually unexpectedly cool things that happened either with or without my doing.
Blessings – For me, that’s usually something I take for granted but that makes my life so much easier.
Successes – For me, that’s usually something I did and that I completed.

In your day, week, month or year.

It’s super easy and I want you to try it.

Make an (unordered) list of all the things that were good. You don’t have to know yet if they’re a highlight, blessing or success. Just make a list and when you go through it again, you can mentally or with a pen categorize each item.

It’s really simple and really fun. I have even started to just mentally go through the day and recap and think about “What were my highlights?”, “What am I blessed with?”, “How did I succeed today?”

Give it a try and see what happens!

text:

Tomás Moyano's story how he and his co-founder used the “Reality Check” methods to deeply understand their market, their customers and run their first successful ad-campaign on LinkedIn.

 Hi, I'm Tomas and I'm an entrepreneur. 
 I work for Hella FastForward and we work on new projects, new ideas for possible startups. 
 We were in the situation that we have an idea we had actually a technical solution to work on and we were trying to find what is a problem that this person had. This was very difficult. 
 What we learned from you and from your workshop – and it was really valuable for us – is to start always with the market or, ideally, with your passion In our situation it was not so easy to start with the passion so we started exploring the market and trying to understand who could be our potential customer? 
 And then from this potential customer we started to understand what what problems do they 
 have? And from having an idea of which products do they have we also wanted to know if they are willing to pay for this? 
 So we start checking if someone advertising to them and then what products do 
 they offer? What type of solution to they offer to the products that they might have? 
 This was really interesting we, learned a lot. We then defined personas and we 
 got very nice results. 
 In fact, we launched three ad campaigns in LinkedIn where we got on average a click-through rate of 1.4 percent. This is supposed to be very good according to LinkedIn average rate. And we also got some leads and the idea now is that since we see that there is some interest in the market we want to contact these leads to learn more about them and the problems. 
 I would recommend this workshop for any entrepreneur that wants to to start a new idea and not start by the technology – that is very tempting to do if you have very good technology – but you don't know if someone wants this it doesn't make any sense because no one will use it or buy it. 
 So thank you very much for this.
 
 Tomás Moyano – Founder Sofa.AI, Berlin, Germany

id: Confidence Is Everything Paul Grahams Startup Curve And The Dunning Kruger Effect.md
text:
Yesterday, I was reading in Grant Cardone’s book “Sell Or Be Sold” and got stuck on the idea that “To the degree that you’re sold yourself on the product, idea, company, service, support you will sell to others. If you’re not 100% sold yourself, you can’t sell to others.”

Could the story of your confidence in your vision be expressed in both, “The Startup Curve” and the Dunning-Kruger effect? Are they potentially the same?

Paul Graham and Trevor Blackwell beautifully and cheekily captured this in “The Startup Curve” sometime around 2008.

What struck me is, how much it reminds me of the Dunning-Kruger effect. I think there’s a correlation because, in the end, what sells and makes a company move forward is utter conviction. That type of motivation is abundant in the beginning but, as we learn more, we get our slices of humble-pie and have to wade through ’the trough of sorrow’ aka. ‘Valley of despair’ until we’re ready to gain wisdom to once again climb the ladder of success.

Anyways, even just for entertainment value, here are the two curves to illustrate:

Source: Blogpost by Andrew Chen, Discussion on HN

title: Confidence Is Everything: Paul Graham's Startup Curve and the Dunning-Kruger Effect

id: I am Shutting Down Internet Access At Home Again (Experiment).md
text:
3 months ago I canceled my internet service at home for two reasons:

1. The service provider sucked and
 
2. I wanted to spend less time online and be less distracted
 

So, for two months I lived without high-speed internet at home.

I read 9 books.

I slept better because no more Netflix or Youtube before bed.

I generally planned my media/information consumption better.

I liked it very much.

I felt freed and less distracted.

But, a month ago I started working on a project with a company in the US.

The time-difference means the time I can interact with the team is from 3pm to 7pm CET.

At that time it became awkward to find a spot to be online, like a cafe or going to the Factory co-working space.

So, I asked my neighbor if she would be so kind to access to her network.\\

She did (thank you very much!) and for the last 3 weeks I’ve been online at home again.

Needless to say, I got sucked back the old habits.

I again checked news, reddit, youtube and wasted hours on Netflix…

So, last night I made a pro/cons list and decided to go offline again.  

But with a twist… It’s not black and white:

I need to access work stuff on my laptop. I have kept the network on my laptop.
 
I like having Alexa there for music. Alexa'll stay online as well.
 
I wasted too much time on my phone. I removed the network from my phone.
 
I wasted far too much time on my iPad. I removed the network from my iPad.

I cut the cords on my phone and iPad yesterday afternoon. 

And I already spent the evening reading again and slept better.
title: Experiment: I'm Shutting Down Internet Access at Home. Again.

text:
A few random thoughts jumbled up and put together. 

Ran the first part of the workshop with Hella this morning and I think it went really well. I enjoyed the questions and how we found our way through trying a bunch of tools until we landed on a few core decisions. 

I’m particularly proud that I held myself back on giving too much judgmental input – As in: When faced with a decision, I asked them what they think makes sense and refused to say what I’d choose – to avoid influencing them. The data should speak for itself. 

A few things: I would probably not go into the market because it’s tiny, enterprisey and hard to find the person that cares the most about it. 

But they’re set on it and they’re being paid a salary so I guess I can understand why they’d go ahead anyways. 

They chose COO as core customer segment #1 which I think isn’t the right one. I think we found that CIOs are much more likely to respond to their message. But they chose COOs so that’s fine. It’s their venture.

So, that I really like.

Gotta make sure I get a good video testimonial from Jonathan, Henry, Soeren, Peer, Tomas and Patrick. That’s actually a really nice list right there. They all have something different to say and I helped them all!

id: This Weeks Challenge Only Positive Thoughts And Actions For 24h.md
text:
In Grant Cardone’s book “Sell Or Be Sold”, he challenges the reader to start a timer and aim to only think and act positively for 24 hours.

There is only one rule:

When a negative, self-limiting belief or action happens, you have to reset the timer and start over.

I’ve challenged myself for a 4 days now.

I’ve “failed” at least 10 times but it’s getting easier and more fun with practice.

Today I finally completed a full 24 hours!

What I like about it:

I enjoy a good challenge.
It’s a lot of fun.
It’s deeply personal.
It has an uplifting, empowering effect on my attitude and outlook.
I’ve become more aware of “head trash” that otherwise sneaks into my head unnoticed.

Plus, It’s easy to try (and no one needs to know.)

All you have to do is simply…

Open your phone’s clock app
Set a timer to 24 hours
Start the timer and focus on positive thoughts and actions
And… if you slip up, reset the timer.
title: This Week's Challenge: “Only positive thoughts and actions for 24h“

For Market Researchers: Social Trends is a free tool that lets you stay ahead of the curve by giving you the fastest growing Meetups in the ‘taste-maker’ cities of New York, Berlin, London and San Francisco.

Trend Watch Focus Berlin

There is a ton of activity in Berlin, Meetups are happening left and right. Over the course of the last year, I’ve seen oodles of fitness, social entrepreneurship and Blockchain-related Meetups come and go.

But today, I would like to share with you a shortlist of interesting communities that have shown consistent growth and strong “gravity” attracting high numbers of members.

Meetup.ai

Started only 8 months ago, Meetup.ai is a community built around Artificial Intelligence. With a consistent growth rate it has attracted 1,422 members to date.

Zero Waste Berlin

A beautiful social movement to reduce waste to zero is a Meetup perfectly suited to Berlin. While “only” 257 members as of today, the constant growth, regardless of seasons, shows how it is a consistent concern to people in Berlin.

If you look at the curve below, you’ll see very smooth and straight growth which makes me think it will continue to grow organically for the coming year. And with that I expect to hear more about Zero Waste in the future!

Token Engineering

The Berlin Token Engineering Meetup is another high-growth community that has attracted over 500 members in the past 6 months. Overall, a nice growth curve with an acceleration between June and September with an otherwise constant trajectory.

With more than a few hundred Blockchain Meetups in Berlin alone, this one stands out by having grown to 500 members around the very technical aspect of the field of token engineering. With this kind of growth I expect this community to continue to thrive and prosper.

So, right now I’m waiting for a re-charge and the experiment will begin by tomorrow morning. I’ll probably write a few more posts on the progress I’m making with the HumanCharger.

id: Why Im A Slow Learner But Fast Performer.md
text:
Over the last year I went on a deep-dive to learn a new skill: How to market and, by extension, how to sell products that I love.

I’ve enjoyed the learning-process. But to be honest, I'm frustrated because my progress has also been slow.

Well, the good news is… I’m finally "getting there” to a point where I can finally perform.

But, maaaaannn, this took much longer than I expected.

This made me think about how I absorb new things…

First off, I’m a total “single-tasker.”

Yet, once I’ve absorbed it, I can speed up execution and perform fast. Over and over again.

I want to believe that – while my enthusiasm goes full Dunning-Kruger – my performance compounds over time.

I see others breeze through what takes me days, weeks and months. It’s hard not to feel down sometimes.

My "slow but steady" learning style has been my mode of operation since University. Instead of taking all required courses, I usually took half the amount.

While half as fast as others, I was usually top of my class in each of the courses I did take.

Well… when I’m learning something new, I can tell that my brain is completely focused and engaged. I can’t think of anything else for that period.

It’s like when you learned to ride a bike.

In the beginning it was hard and slow. You gotta keep your balance, move your feet, steer with your hands.

It required full attention and time to practice and “sink in.”

Then, with a little bit of consistent practice it got easier and required less attention. To the point where you don’t have to think about it but do.

So, long story short. I’ve learned a lot this year. It took me much longer than I expected.

It’s been very frustrating...

But I’m also noticing how it’s becoming easier and easier every day.
title: Why I’m a Slow Learner But Fast Performer

id: How To Discover What You Really Need The Most With The Needs Card Deck.md
text:
I totally forgot to mention this, but I made a card deck last year that has helped me explore and discover needs as part of my personal development.

I’ve used the deck to rapidly and easily identify and understand those parts of my life that were either helping me move forward or that were holding me back emotionally.

It's also a radically insightful tool for...

Relationship Development
Customer Needs Research
Design Research

In short, the cards are like "Google Maps for Your Needs and Feelings”

The list comprises of about 50-60 core needs published at Center of Non-Violent Communication’s website which has the following (incomplete) list of needs and desires:

<table<tbody<tr<td<div<bCONNECTION</b</div<divacceptance</div<divaffection</div<divappreciation</div<divbelonging</div<divcooperation</div<divcommunication</div<divcloseness</div<divcommunity</div<divcompanionship</div<divcompassion</div<divconsideration</div<divconsistency</div<divempathy</div<divinclusion</div<divintimacy</div<divlove</div<divmutuality</div<divnurturing</div<divrespect/self-respect</div<divsafety</div<divsecurity</div<divstability</div<divsupport</div<divto know and be known</div<divto see and be seen</div<divto understand and be understood</div<divtrust</div</td<td<div<bPHYSICAL WELLBEING</b</div<divwarmth</div<divair</div<divfood</div<divmovement/exercise</div<divrest/sleep</div<divsexual expression</div<divsafety</div<divshelter</div<divtouch</div<divwater</div<div<bHONESTY </b</div<divauthenticity</div<divintegrity</div<divpresence</div<div<bPLAY </b</div<divjoy</div<divhumor</div<div<bPEACE </b</div<divbeauty</div<divcommunion</div<divease</div<divequality</div<divharmony</div<divinspiration</div<divorder</div<div<bAUTONOMY </b</div<divchoice</div<divfreedom</div<divindependence</div<divspace</div<divspontaneity</div</td<td<div<bMEANING</b</div<divawareness</div<divcelebration of life</div<divchallenge</div<divclarity</div<divcompetence</div<divconsciousness</div<divcontribution</div<divcreativity</div<divdiscovery</div<divefficacy</div<diveffectiveness</div<divgrowth</div<divhope</div<divlearning</div<divmourning</div<divparticipation</div<divpurpose</div<divselfexpression</div<divstimulation</div<divto matter</div<divunderstanding</div</td</tr</tbody</table

(© 2005 by Center for Nonviolent Communication Website: www.cnvc.org Email: cnvc@cnvc.org Phone: +1.505-244-4041)

Why Use Needs As a Starting Point For Personal Development?

A major reason to use these “Needs” as my starting point for personal investigations was that, according to one school of thought, emotions (positive and negative ones) are always the result of an important need that’s either met (positive feelings) or unmet (negative feelings.)

Universal Needs, Individual Responses

Furthermore, while needs are relatively universal, the individual response to them are highly individual. I find this deeply fascinating.

For example, if I’m currently in need of community and that need is met, I may feel positively calm.

Someone else may feel positively excited for the same reason.

If my need for community isn’t met, I may feel negatively frustrated while someone else may feel negatively bored:

So, to better understand my emotions (and my actions that come from them) I use the inventory of needs to navigate an otherwise complex ball of golden twine also know as my psyche.

There are a bunch of ways to use the cards, but I’ve found two that work the best for me.

Strategy 1: Drive By Intuition

The first one is simply to spread out the cards unsorted and start to pick out those cards that I intuitively respond to. Once I’ve found a handful or so needs that I’m interested in, I start to discuss them with a partner or coach or simply with myself.

The main questions then are:

Is this a met or unmet need?
How does it make me feel?
If it’s an unmet need, what can I do to change that?

The last question can quickly drive out an action I can take today to make my life better.

Strategy #2: Dump and Sort

The second strategy is even simpler and just as effective to get to a selection of met, unmet and irrelevant needs:

For each card, I ask myself:

Is this an important, met need?
Is this an important, unmet need?
Is this an irrelevant need at the moment?

Going through each card, I wind up with three stacks: MET, UNMET and IRRELEVANT.

I then focus on the UNMET needs again because they contribute to my feeling the most unease and devise action items to solve them.

Needs are Values

I never really connected with when people, and more often, companies, talked what their values. It just seemed so abstract. Co-incidentally, discovering important needs also becomes the list of my personal values. Things that I value above all else.

Still got a few packs

Sorry, all sold out at the moment!

Last but not least, I still have a few packs that I produced last year. If you’re ready to turn on your own “Google Maps to Your Psyche” and discover and understand yourself more deeply, let me know. I’m selling them for $47 per pack.

Just shoot me an email at Alexis dot Rondeau at Gmail dot com and, if I still have a set, I’ll mail it to you.

Cheers!

text:
Wednesday afternoon, at home, not crazy about being here but I think I’m dragging out the cold I got over a week ago, so I took a nap just now and feel better. Didn’t feel up to bar at all this morning and still went on a nice bike-ride with my dad. We visited Factory which I decided isn’t a place that I want to go to anymore. 

I also realized, based on my father’s observation, that the vibe of people sitting alongside long tables in silence at their computers totally feels like a factory. That they look like factory workers, quietly typing along and not talking to each other. 

I guess that’s one of the reasons I’ve felt so alienated there for so long. I just couldn’t put my finger on it. 

So, I think it’ll be best to cancel my subscription this week and avoid paying another $130 per month for a place that I don’t enjoy. I’ll be able to put that money towards things that give me joy and move me forward. It’s kinda sad because the Factory building is really nice. But I also realized that the endless amount of heavy doors you have to open and close to get from A to B really disrupts my flow of thinking and working. 

I also think I will cancel my Drip.com subscription and the Javelin.com subscription, too. In both cases I can use other, cheaper services. I will keep my Clickfunnels subscription because that’s been really working well. It’s a good tool and I’m learning a lot with it. For Drip I can use Mailchimp for which I still have an account. For Javelin I’m already using Evernote instead. 

What else? 

What would I like to share today? Brainstorm...

 Birthday dinner
 
 Taking care of yourself when you’ve got a cold
 

 Getting better after a cold took much longer than I expected. I’m on day 10 and still don’t feel 100%.
 
 I had felt a cold coming up first on Wednesday, two weeks ago. I felt weak and I noticed how I couldn’t concentrate. Then, that Thursday I felt okay again. Weaker than usual but I didn’t mind. Thursday night I had a sore throat though and that led me to believe that I was about to crash. Which brings us today where I’m back home and though I wish I was more productive, I’m also glad to be here and probably going to take another nap before going for dinner with my dad. I thought I had rested enough about a week ago and was on the mend but I’m still not feeling 100%. So that’s a big learning for me. It takes much more time to feel and be back to normal than I expected. I could have used a 10X massive care-taking action instead of just doing the absolute minimum and hope I’m better soon. Good insight.
